headline: Responsibilities are what you owe—obligations to yourself, others, and the world you share
universal_truth: Rights and responsibilities are inseparable; claiming one requires honoring the other
fun_facts: Every right implies a corresponding responsibility—freedom of speech requires responsible speech
Responsibility comes from the Latin 'respondere'—to respond or answer
Mature societies balance individual rights with collective responsibilities
discussion_questions: What responsibilities do you take seriously?
How do you balance what you owe yourself versus others?
What happens when people claim rights without accepting responsibilities?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Rights are what you're owed. Responsibilities are what you owe. Yesterday we explored rights; today we flip the coin. What do you owe others? What do you owe yourself? What do you owe the world you share?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: It's tempting to focus on rights without responsibilities. But why are they inseparable?

options.text: Responsibilities complete the social contract—rights only work when others fulfill responsibilities; your right to safety requires others' responsibility not to harm; rights and duties are two sides of one coin
options.response: Yes. Rights exist in relationship. Your right implies someone's duty. Claiming rights while ignoring responsibilities is taking without giving—it collapses the system that makes rights possible.

options.text: Responsibilities are just obligations imposed on us
options.response: Some are imposed, but many are chosen—responsibilities to those we love, commitments we make...

q1.title: To Self and Others
q1.script: Responsibilities extend in all directions: to yourself (taking care of your wellbeing), to others (honoring commitments), to community (contributing to shared life). Each domain matters.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "To Self and Others"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Chosen and Inherited
q2.script: Some responsibilities are chosen—promises you make, roles you accept. Others are inherited—family, citizenship, humanity. Both are real. The key is conscious acceptance.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Reliability Matters
q3.script: Responsibility is meaningless without follow-through. What you say you'll do, do. Reliability in responsibility builds trust. Broken promises erode social fabric.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Rights and responsibilities are inseparable. Claiming one requires honoring the other. Accept what you owe.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 331. Tomorrow, we'll explore being part of a place—citizenship. Until then, consider what you owe and whether you're delivering.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Responsibility Audit - What Do You Owe?
growTrack.activity: List your responsibilities—to yourself, to specific people, to your community. Which are you fulfilling well? Which are you neglecting? Choose one responsibility to strengthen this week.
